correctness.rationale: For n=prod p^{a_p}, D(n)/n=sum a_p/p, and integrality D(n)/n=k forces p|a_p for each p by reducing n|D(n) modulo p^{a_p}; conversely if a_p=p c_p then sum c_p=k. Thus all solutions come from a composition of k into r<=k positive integers. Leading r=k solutions have c_p=1 and log n=sum_{j=1}^k p_j log p_j with distinct primes. By PNT, B(L)=#{p:p log p<=L}~L/(log L)^2, regularly varying index 1. Product weak convergence on simplex sum t_i<=1 yields k-fold ordered volume 1/k!, and division by k! distinct permutations gives B(L)^k/(k!)^2. Repeated primes and r<k solutions O(B(L)^{k-1}), so A_k(x)~(log x)^k/[(k!)^2(loglog x)^{2k}] for fixed positive integer k. Independent direct exact sieve enumerated n<=1,400,000 for k=1..4 and agreed structural equivalence; this does not prove the analytic limit.

value.rationale: The arithmetic derivative's integer logarithmic-derivative fibers are a natural number-theoretic classification. Exact asymptotics with leading constants for every fixed k and concentration on maximal distinct prime support add meaningful distribution information to the previously known k=1 solution and exponent divisibility criterion; prime-weight simplex counting is a substantive analytic step.

limitations: Only fixed positive integer k as x->infinity; no uniformity for growing k or rational nonintegral multipliers.
Finite census not an asymptotic proof; proof depends on standard prime number theorem and convergence of regularly varying counting measures.
